title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
statement:
Given a binary search tree (BST) and two nodes in the tree, find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of the two nodes.

The lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a BST is the deepest node that is an ancestor of both nodes. A node can be its own ancestor.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [2, 10^5]
Both p and q exist in the BST

visibleExamples.explanation: The LCA of nodes 2 and 8 is 6.
The LCA of nodes 2 and 4 is 2, since a node can be its own ancestor.

jsonFriendlyReason: Requires TreeNode adapter for root, p, and q parameters; return type is TreeNode
